children: Shareholders back four independent directors and one non-executive director as Zee outlines governance and growth priorities

Zee Entertainment Enterprises shareholders have approved the reappointment of five directors at the company’s 44th Annual General Meeting held on Thursday, with the resolutions receiving the requisite majority.
Deepu Bansal, Uttam Prakash Agarwal, P.V. Ramana Murthy and Shishir Babubhai Desai were reappointed as Independent Directors, while Saurav Adhikari was reappointed as a Non-Executive Director.
The company said the shareholder support would help the Board continue to strengthen governance standards, guide the management team on strategic priorities and focus on stakeholder value.

Speaking at the AGM, Chairman R. Gopalan said the Board was maintaining oversight of the company’s strategic priorities to ensure that growth capital was deployed effectively. Gopalan added that Zee was working to build a technology-powered digital ecosystem to monitor existing policies and internal processes.
The system is expected to create an internal intelligence warehouse to track key business activities and strengthen accountability in response to stakeholder expectations and regulatory requirements.
Gopakalan also highlighted the need for greater transparency and disclosures to give stakeholders a clearer understanding of Zee’s progress on its strategic priorities.

Chief Executive Officer Punit Goenka said Zee was building a more diversified portfolio as it seeks to capture a larger share of the attention economy. The company is developing new growth engines in areas including micro dramas, kids content and live entertainment.
Goenka also said Zee’s partnership with global animation and visual effects studio PhantomFX would support the development of intellectual property in animated content.

Zee’s sports strategy is focused on building a sustainable sports ecosystem in India while driving engagement through major sporting properties. The company is looking to build engagement around properties including FIFA, Bundesliga and Serie A, alongside on-ground initiatives aimed at supporting sports.
Gopalan said the company remained focused on long-term value creation and noted that Zee had declared a dividend of Rs 2 per equity share despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.
